text: Olton Willem van Genderen (17 October 1921 – 9 November 1990) was a Surinamese civil servant and politician who served as Deputy Prime Minister of Suriname from 24 December 1973 until the coup d'état of 25 February 1980. He was one of the main negotiators for Suriname's independence. Born on 17 October 1921 in Albina, he worked for the customs agency and, in the 1950s, went to Rotterdam for four years where he became a licensed customs officer. He became active in trade unions and politics and was given the honorary title Da Djendé (Ndyuka: Beautiful teacher). In 1958, he was first elected to the Estates of Suriname and was re-elected five times. On 16 May 1967, he was elected Chairman of the Estates of Suriname, serving until 1 September 1969. On 15 December 1973, he was re-elected as Chairman, but resigned on 28 December because he had been elected Deputy Prime Minister on 24 December in the Arron cabinet. He also served as Minister of District Administration and Decentralisation. The Arron government negotiated with the Dutch government regarding Suriname's independence, and van Genderen was a key negotiator. On 25 November 1975, Suriname gained independence. In 1977, he was appointed Minister of the Interior, the successor to the Ministry of District Administration and Decentralisation. On 25 February 1980, Desi Bouterse carried out a coup d'état; Arron went into hiding, while van Genderen was captured. On 26 February, van Genderen and Minister Badrising announced the government's surrender on television, urging the population not to resist the military regime. On 28 February, Arron surrendered to the regime. Van Genderen was placed under house arrest until February 1981. On 19 June 1981, he was sentenced to four months imprisonment minus time served under house arrest and fined a total of ƒ 55,000. Van Genderen died on 9 November 1990 at the age of 69. In 2021, the Emmastraat in Albina was renamed Olton Willem van Genderen Boulevard in his honor.
